questions.prompt: Directions : Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on a campus event that has impressed them most. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.correctAnswer:
The campus event that impressed me most was a student-organized charity book fair. It took place last term and showed me how a small idea could connect learning with care for others.

Before the event, volunteers collected books from students and teachers, sorted them by subject and checked their condition. On the day of the fair, readers could choose useful books at low prices. The organizers clearly explained how the money would support a community reading project and displayed the records afterward. I helped at one stall and was surprised by how many visitors stayed to discuss books rather than simply buy them.

What impressed me was not the size of the event, but the cooperation behind it. Different students contributed practical skills, and transparency made their effort trustworthy. The fair reminded me that meaningful campus activities can create opportunities to learn, share resources and strengthen our sense of community.

questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。慈善书展有准备、活动、透明记录与个人参与，结尾回到合作带来的印象；这是原创事件设定。

首段选定印象最深的慈善书展，主体用准备、参与和透明记录描述事件，结尾解释合作和共享为什么打动自己。campus event是校园活动，raise funds是筹款，take responsibility是承担责任。过去时记述经历，个人体会可用现在时。不必罗列许多活动：一件具体事件配细节更容易说清impressed most。范文为原创示范，金额、人物和日期不当作真实学校数据。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约150词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——选择一件最有印象的校园活动，描述经过并解释触动你的原因。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

questions.prompt: One consequence of climate change is that some people may not have adequate access to certain foods.
questions.passage:
How Climate Change Will Affect What You Eat

A) Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct(灭绝的) due to climate change. Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too?

B) It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. By using the genes from resurrection(复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.

C) But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. Despite alarmist headlines about "foods that are going extinct," there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.

D) But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food. We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. "Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the US Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office. In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.

E) Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30℃ is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean(大豆) production in the US show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold(临界点).

B) It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. By using the genes from resurrection(复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.

C) But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. Despite alarmist headlines about "foods that are going extinct," there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.

D) But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food. We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. "Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the US Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office. In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.

E) Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30℃ is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean(大豆) production in the US show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold(临界点).

F) In the US—the world's largest producer of corn and soybeans—farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says. But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of Iowa declines in quality—a legacy of glacial(冰川的) expansion. Other studies, including studies of wheat in India and corn in Africa, also found that there is a threshold above which yields sharply decline: crops can adapt and move, but only to a point. "What's common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop," Schlenker says. "If predictions for the end of the century are true, though, I think a lot of agricultural areas in the US will see significant hits."

K) Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places, including applying more fertiliser, implementing better irrigation, using machinery that gets crops out of the field faster or installing storage facilities to delay spoilage. "Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist," Walsh says. "General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes."

"We've seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue," M Jarvis says. 中国政府十分重视人民的健康饮食(diet)。通过大力提倡健康饮食，人们对合理营养增进健康的重要性有了更加深刻的认识。"吃得安全、吃得营养、吃得健康"是人民对美好生活的基本需要，是提升人民幸福感的必然要求，也为食品产业的发展提供了新机遇。目前，各级政府都在采取多种举措确保人民饮食健康，推进健康中国的建设。
questions.correctAnswer: The Chinese government attaches great importance to a healthy diet. By vigorously promoting healthy eating, it has helped people gain a deeper understanding of the importance of proper nutrition in improving health. Eating safely, nutritiously and healthily is a basic need in people's pursuit of a better life and an essential requirement for increasing their happiness. It also offers new opportunities for the development of the food industry. At present, governments at all levels are taking various measures to ensure healthy diets and advance the building of a healthy China.
questions.referenceAnswer: The Chinese government attaches great importance to a healthy diet. By vigorously promoting healthy eating, it has helped people gain a deeper understanding of the importance of proper nutrition in improving health. Eating safely, nutritiously and healthily is a basic need in people's pursuit of a better life and an essential requirement for increasing their happiness. It also offers new opportunities for the development of the food industry. At present, governments at all levels are taking various measures to ensure healthy diets and advance the building of a healthy China.
questions.hint: 安全、营养、健康是并列要求；幸福和产业机会均需保留。
questions.explanation:
以下译文为原创参考，可使用其他准确表达。proper nutrition不是仅吃得多；governments at all levels对应各级政府；最后的健康中国建设不可省略。

逐句核对：healthy diet与proper nutrition分别饮食健康和合理营养，gain a deeper understanding是认识深化。Eating safely, nutritiously and healthily三个副词平行，对应吃得安全、营养、健康。basic need、essential requirement、new opportunities分别美好生活需要、幸福感要求、产业机会，三层不能只留一句。governments at all levels为各级政府，various measures保留多种举措，advance the building of a healthy China传达末句目标。
